title: Unpivot Squad Match Stats by Month
prompt: You are working with a battle royale mobile game that tracks squad match completion and invites. The squad_monthly_stats table stores monthly match counts for each squad across three game modes in wide format (columns for_solo_count, for_duo_count, for_squad_count). Each monthly snapshot row also includes the squad_name (which may have extra whitespace), the month as a VARCHAR date like '2024-01-15', and an array of active_regions where the squad played that month. Write a query that unpivots this wide table into long format with one row per (squad, month, game_mode) combination. The output must have columns: squad_id, squad_name (cleaned: trimmed and title-cased), month_label (the full month name from the month date, e.g. 'January'), game_mode (the literal label for each unpivoted column: 'Solo' for_solo_count, 'Duo' for_duo_count, 'Squad' for_squad_count), match_count (the numeric value from the unpivoted column, rounded to the nearest integer), and primary_region (the first element of the active_regions array). Exclude any rows where the match count is NULL. Order the results by squad_id ASC, then game_mode ASC, then month_label ASC (chronologically: January before February, etc.).

display.context: You are working with a battle royale mobile game that tracks squad match completion and invites.
display.task: Write a query that unpivots the squad_monthly_stats table from wide format (separate columns per game mode) to long format with one row per (squad, month, game_mode) combination.

table_notes.squad_monthly_stats: stores monthly match counts for each squad across three game modes (solo, duo, squad) in wide format, along with squad name, month date, and active regions

output_field_notes.squad_id: the unique identifier for the squad
output_field_notes.squad_name: the name of the squad, cleaned and formatted
output_field_notes.month_label: the full name of the month from the stored date
output_field_notes.game_mode: the game mode label (Solo, Duo, or Squad) corresponding to the unpivoted column
output_field_notes.match_count: the number of matches completed in that mode and month, rounded to the nearest integer
output_field_notes.primary_region: the first region from the squad's active regions array for that month

field_logic: squad_name: take the raw squad name, remove leading and trailing whitespace, and capitalize each word
month_label: extract the full month name from the month date string (convert to date first, then format as full month name)
game_mode: assign the literal label 'Solo' for the solo count column, 'Duo' for the duo count column, and 'Squad' for the squad count column
match_count: take the numeric value from each unpivoted column and round it to the nearest whole number
primary_region: extract the first element from the active regions array (arrays are 1-indexed)
edge_cases: If a match count column contains NULL, exclude that row from the output.
If the month date is stored as text, convert it to a date type before extracting the month name.
display.filter_note: Only rows where the unpivoted match count is not NULL are included.
display.order_by_note: Results are ordered by squad_id ascending, then game_mode ascending (alphabetically: Duo, Solo, Squad), then month_label ascending (chronologically: January, February, etc.).

schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE squad_monthly_stats (squad_id INT, squad_name VARCHAR(100), month VARCHAR(20), solo_count DECIMAL(10,2), duo_count DECIMAL(10,2), squad_count DECIMAL(10,2), active_regions TEXT[]);

composite_moves: reshape (unpivot: UNION ALL of 3 SELECTs, one per game mode column, each with literal label)
NULL filter (WHERE IS NOT NULL on unpivoted value)
multi-level ORDER BY (squad_id, game_mode, month name in chronological order via CASE)

hints: PostgreSQL does not have a native UNPIVOT command; you need to manually stack the columns using UNION ALL, with one SELECT per game mode column.

Each SELECT in the UNION ALL should include a literal string for the game_mode ('Solo', 'Duo', 'Squad') and pull the corresponding count column. Add a WHERE clause to each branch to exclude NULL counts.

To order by month name chronologically, use a CASE expression in the ORDER BY clause that maps month names to numeric positions (January = 1, February = 2, March = 3, etc.). Wrap the entire UNION ALL in a subquery so you can apply ORDER BY with the CASE expression.
answer_key: SELECT squad_id, INITCAP(TRIM(squad_name)) AS squad_name, TO_CHAR(month::DATE, 'FMMonth') AS month_label, game_mode, ROUND(match_count) AS match_count, active_regions[1] AS primary_region FROM (SELECT squad_id, squad_name, month, 'Solo' AS game_mode, solo_count AS match_count, active_regions FROM squad_monthly_stats WHERE solo_count IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT squad_id, squad_name, month, 'Duo' AS game_mode, duo_count AS match_count, active_regions FROM squad_monthly_stats WHERE duo_count IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT squad_id, squad_name, month, 'Squad' AS game_mode, squad_count AS match_count, active_regions FROM squad_monthly_stats WHERE squad_count IS NOT NULL) AS unpivoted ORDER BY squad_id ASC, game_mode ASC, CASE TO_CHAR(month::DATE, 'FMMonth') WHEN 'January' THEN 1 WHEN 'February' THEN 2 WHEN 'March' THEN 3 WHEN 'April' THEN 4 WHEN 'May' THEN 5 WHEN 'June' THEN 6 WHEN 'July' THEN 7 WHEN 'August' THEN 8 WHEN 'September' THEN 9 WHEN 'October' THEN 10 WHEN 'November' THEN 11 WHEN 'December' THEN 12 END ASC;
